channel.title: Business Insider Africa - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Business Insider Africa (africa.businessinsider.com)

item.title: From mines to vaults: DR Congo to channel state-traded gold into central bank reserves
item.description: The DR Congo's central bank - Banque Centrale du Congo (BCC) has unveiled a strategic move to deepen economic sovereignty, announcing plans to purchase gold directly from DRC Gold Trading SA, a fully state-owned company aggregating output from artisanal and small-scale miners.

item.title: 10 African countries with the highest fuel prices in February 2026
item.description: High gasoline prices are still one of the most persistent economic pressure points in African countries, influencing inflation patterns, household welfare, and company competitiveness.

item.title: Egypt discovers 4,300-year-old body wrapped in pure gold inside limestone coffin
item.description: Archaeologists in Egypt have uncovered a 4,300-year-old mummy wrapped in gold inside a sealed limestone coffin at the Saqqara necropolis, south of Cairo, in a discovery that highlights the enduring link between gold, power and belief in one of Africa’s most historically influential civilisations.

item.title: Magda Wierzycka launches new AI venture fund in South Africa
item.description: Magda Wierzycka, the co-founder and CEO of Sygnia Ltd, is preparing to launch a new venture capital fund to support South African startups working in artificial intelligence. She is widely known as the richest woman in South Africa and one of its most successful business leaders.

item.title: Naguib Sawiris Reveals €500 Million Loss After Emotional Investment
item.description: Egyptian businessman Naguib Sawiris recently shared a surprising lesson he learned the hard way: he once lost about €500 million because he made an investment while angry.

item.title: Africa’s fifth weakest military negotiates $900 million deal for 24 Pakistan JF-17 fighter jets
item.description: Somalia, ranked among the world’s weakest militaries, is negotiating with Pakistan to acquire up to 24 JF-17 Thunder Block III fighter jets in what could mark its most significant defence investment in decades, according to Defence Security Asia.

item.title: 8 African economies facing heightened global scrutiny over money laundering controls in February 2026
item.description: Eight African economies are currently under “increased monitoring” by the Financial Action Task Force as of 13 February 2026, a designation widely referred to as the grey list.

item.title: Ghana and Burkina Faso seal seven deals to secure West Africa’s key trade corridor
item.description: Ghana and Burkina Faso have moved to strengthen diplomatic and security cooperation, signing seven bilateral agreements aimed at stabilising one of West Africa’s most sensitive trade and security corridors.

item.title: Nigeria in focus as top US counter-terror finance official begins high-stakes visit
item.description: The United States is ramping up security cooperation with Nigeria as Jonathan Burke, Washington’s Assistant Secretary for Terrorist Financing, prepares for a two-day visit aimed at tightening safeguards against illicit funding networks.

item.title: South Africa races to save 134-year-old sugar giant with 2 million-ton milling capacity from shutdown
item.description: South Africa’s government is stepping into the unfolding crisis at Tongaat Hulett, one of the country’s oldest and largest sugar producers, warning of potentially severe consequences for jobs, farmers, and the broader sugar industry.
